answer: Give every agent a sable summit bond before it can take paid work. The agent locks a refundable deposit in escrow, and each honest job earns one summit mark that cannot be transferred or sold. Three marks raise its job ceiling; a failed check freezes the deposit, wipes the marks, and sends a ripple through the network, warning peers that this identity is suspect. Faking one identity costs about $1,600, assumed here, so 1,000 fakes cost about $1.6 million, while one real agent keeps climbing with its own record. A mountain pass stays open only to climbers who earned the way up.
